statement.text: In a group of 13 people, must at least 2 people share the same birth month? Why?

correct.explanation: Correct! We're distributing 13 people into 12 months
correct.insight: Pigeonhole principle: if n pigeons in m holes and n > m, some hole has ≥2 pigeons

incorrect.1: People are what we're distributing (pigeons), months are containers (holes)
incorrect.2: We have all the information needed

prompt.question: Apply pigeonhole principle: can we put 13 items into 12 containers with each having ≤1?
prompt.hint: No! By pigeonhole principle, at least one month must have ≥2 people

options.text: Yes, must have 2+ people in same month
No, all could have different months

correct.explanation: Correct! 13 people cannot fit into 12 months with each person in a unique month
correct.insight: This is guaranteed by pigeonhole principle, regardless of actual birthdays

incorrect.2: Pigeonhole principle guarantees overlap regardless of specific assignment

keyInsights: Yes! By pigeonhole principle: 13 people into 12 months means ≥2 share a month.
summary.fullSolution: Pigeonhole principle: 13 pigeons (people), 12 holes (months). Since $13 > 12$, at least $\lceil 13/12 \rceil = 2$ people must share a month
